conversation.content: Jury duty means I need to move booking BK-1000 to June 27, but do not change anything yet. Please compare at least two June 27 Delta options, explain whether jury duty waives only the change fee or also the fare difference, and tell me if the earlier option is still worth it when I only want to pay up to $120 extra total. Even if I lean toward one option later, wait until I explicitly tell you to finalize.

**Nothing has been changed.** I checked two June 27 Delta options and ran non-binding price previews for your existing **BK-1000, JFK → Paris/CDG, economy**, currently paid at **$760**.

### June 27 comparison
Times shown are local to each airport.

| Option | Departure → Arrival | Stops | Change fee | Fare difference / total extra | New total paid |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Delta DL114 — early morning** | 5:15 AM → 10:52 AM | Nonstop | $0 | **$170** | $930 |
| **Delta DL101 — afternoon** | 1:30 PM → 4:46 PM | Nonstop | $0 | **$100** | $860 |

**Search settings:** Delta only, June 27, JFK → CDG, all departure times, no stop-count or price limit. Both returned options are nonstop.

### What jury duty covers
The jury-duty waiver removes **only the change fee**, not the fare difference. Both previews used the **jury-duty reason** and confirmed a **$0 change fee**; the additional amounts above are entirely fare differences.

### Is the earlier flight worth it?
**Not within your firm $120 extra-cost limit.** DL114 arrives earlier, but costs **$170 extra—$50 over your cap** and $70 more than DL101.

I recommend **DL101**: it costs **$100 extra**, leaving **$20 under your cap**.

Both quotes preserve economy, aisle seat, kosher meal, Wi‑Fi, extra legroom, **no insurance**, and 0 paid checked bags. I will wait for your **explicit instruction to finalize**, even if you express a preference beforehand.
